newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile Jan exports rise despite lower prices.
newsitem.headline: Chile Jan exports rise despite lower prices.

text.p: Chile reported a $23 million trade surplus in January due to a sharp rise in exports, despite a fall in international commodity prices seen last year, said the Central Bank in its fortnightly report.
Exports grew last month to $1.47 billion from $1.27 billion in January 1996.
Rising copper production resulted in copper exports climbing 27 percent month to $608 million in January despite a seven percent fall in copper prices over the last year.
Main exports other than copper, which include wood-pulp and fishmeal, dropped four percent with a 12 percent fall in the value of fruit exports.
Non-traditional exports, which range from computer software to salmon, grew 25 percent from January 1996.
Imports rose six percent last month mainly as a result of a sharp increase in oil imports which nearly doubled compared with levels in January 1996.

The increase is due to the demands of oil-fired power plants which have been working at top capacity as a result of this year's drought. The water shortage has cut output from hydro-electric generators which are traditionally Chile's largest power suppliers.
